name: Nickel-Expanse
geological_features: Flat nickel-rich plains stretching thousands of kilometers
Magnetic pole anomalies creating aurora displays
Tectonic rift valleys at the continental margins
specific_features: Derelict space station in decaying orbit
description: Nickel-Expanse is a world of vast, flat horizons where the eye can travel uninterrupted for hundreds of kilometers across shimmering metallic plains. The nickel-rich soil gives the landscape a distinctive grey-green hue, and the planet's strong magnetic field generates spectacular auroral displays that paint the night sky in curtains of emerald and violet. Shallow seas separate three major continental plates, their waters tinted faintly green by dissolved minerals.

The flatness of the terrain creates an oppressive sense of exposure, as though the entire world is a stage with no wings to retreat to. Winds sweep unimpeded across the plains, carrying a fine metallic dust that coats everything in a grey-green patina. The auroras are visible even during twilight hours, giving the sky a restless, living quality that makes the emptiness feel less lonely.

A terraforming initiative begun two centuries ago was partially abandoned when funding collapsed, leaving atmospheric processors running at reduced capacity. The native fauna, large grazing animals adapted to the metallic plains, have been declining since the atmospheric composition began shifting. A derelict space station, once the project's orbital hub, circles overhead in a slowly decaying orbit, its automated systems still broadcasting status reports to an agency that no longer exists.

The terraforming equipment could be restored to full operation with sufficient investment, potentially transforming this world into a major agricultural colony. However, doing so would likely doom the remaining native species, creating a moral dilemma that has paralyzed decision-making. The derelict station's orbit will decay within the decade, and its uncontrolled re-entry could scatter radioactive debris across the northern plains.
